subject: Security qualification: SOC 2 DDQ, audit logs, and retention next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security qualification: SOC 2 DDQ, audit logs, and retention next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick write-up from our side so your security team has a single place to reference what we discussed and the next steps we agreed on. Please tell me if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Regulatory requirement: 7+ years of transactional retention for audit (some datasets are subject to 7-10 year holds).
- Need for proof of controls (SOC 2) and examples of audit logs to validate retention + access controls.
- Encryption and keying: primary ask whether keys can be customer-managed (KMS/HSM).
- Pen test expectations: scope and evidence cadence for third-party pen test results.

Goals we identified:
1) Satisfy AcroPay’s security gate to proceed to a pilot (PII-handling endpoints isolated, retention policy validated).
2) Confirm DPA language around retention and subprocessor list.
3) Provide artifacts for initial risk review (SOC 2 report, sample audit logs, architecture diagram).

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- Naomi: Send SOC 2 summary + link to complete report (we will redact sensitive client names) — by EOD 3/10. [attachment: redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf]
- Ben: Prepare a 24-72 hour sample of audit-log exports (CSV) with schema notes — by 3/11. [attachment: audit-log-sample.csv]
- Jordan: Draft DPA response / push redline to AcroPay legal and share DocuSign link — by 3/12. [attachment: DPA_redline_v1.docx]
- Sam / AcroPay: Confirm whether the retention window varies by dataset and share the compliance reviewer contact for follow-up.

A couple of clarifying notes from the call:
- Our audit log architecture stores immutable append-only event streams; retention is configurable per-tenant and can be set to meet regulatory windows. We frequently provide a CSV export for audit teams and can map fields to your canonical schema.
- For customer-managed keys, we integrate with common KMS providers; we can scope an HSM option if your procurement requires it (will need legal & infra sign-off).

Attachments included as stubs for intake: redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf, audit-log-sample.csv, DPA_redline_v1.docx.

If that aligns, I’ll circle back with the redlines and the audit-log sample next.

Thanks —
Naomi

From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acropay.com>

Subject: Re: Security qualification: SOC 2 DDQ, audit logs, and retention next steps

Naomi —

Appreciate the concise recap. Confirming a few items from our side:
1) Retention windows: different datasets have different windows. Transactional ledgers require 7 years; authentication logs require 2 years. Legal will confirm a final matrix but we can start with the 7-year requirement as the gating item.
2) SOC 2: please send the most recent report and any summary of in-scope systems. Redactions are fine.
3) Audit logs: we prefer examples in CSV + a short mapping doc (field -> meaning). Ideally we can run a small sanity check with our compliance tooling.
4) KMS/HSM: yes, we require a customer-managed KMS option for production. If HSM is supported, include notes on attestation and key rotation cadence.
5) Pen testing: our procurement will require evidence of a recent third-party pen test and a plan for annual tests (or evidence of similar cadence).

Could you also confirm whether Redwood's hosted environment supports a per-tenant retention policy that can be asserted in the DPA? If not, we’ll need to discuss Dedicated or Private deployment options.

We’ll get the compliance reviewer (Maya Gomez) looped in early next week — I’ll share the contact once Legal confirms. For now, thank you for the artifacts — looking forward to the audit-log CSV.

Best,
Sam
Sam Taylor
Head of Security, AcroPay
sam.taylor@acropay.com

Sam / Naomi —

Following up with some technical context on the audit logs and KMS support so you can circulate to AcroPay's tooling team:

Audit logs (what we’ll provide)
- Format: gzipped CSV export (UTF-8) with a simple header row. I attached a small sample that mirrors production fields (timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, user_id, resource, action, result_code, ip, user_agent).
- Retention: configurable per-tenant. For hosted customers we set a default of 90 days hot, then up to multi-year cold storage (S3 Glacier or equivalent). We can pin retention to 7 years for a tenant in our config; for retrieval we provide both export and temporary read-backed access.

KMS / HSM
- KMS: customer-managed KMS is supported via AWS KMS and GCP KMS; keys are used to encrypt dataset master keys.
- HSM: for Dedicated or Private deployments we can integrate with HSM-backed key stores; for hosted we can discuss a Bring-Your-Key pattern with an HSM-backed KMS provider (procurement/legal appetite required).

Pen test evidence
- We run annual third-party penetration tests and can share redacted reports and remediation summaries.

Next practical items I’ll deliver by EOD 3/11:
- audit-log-sample.csv (attached)
- field_mapping.md (short mapping notes; link included in Drive folder)

Ben
